title: Creating a Cloud SQL Decoy in GCP

blocks.text: The cloud SQL in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is a service that allows you to set up and host relational databases (MySQL or PostgreSQL). You can create cloud SQL decoy databases (public or private) based on MySQL or PostgreSQL to lure adversaries that are looking for databases to disrupt services or steal data. Optionally, the credentials of the master user (or root) of the database along with the URL can be added to a landmine policy as a lure. You can view and analyze the attack details from the Zscaler Deception dashboard.
Before creating a cloud SQL decoy in GCP, ensure that you have configured the integration between GCP and Deception.
To create a cloud SQL decoy:

blocks.item: Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Cloud SQL.
Click Add Decoy.
See image.
The GCP Cloud SQL drawer appears.
In the GCP Cloud SQL drawer:
Project: Select the project in which you want to create the decoy.
Name: Enter a name for the cloud SQL database decoy.
Description: Enter a description for the cloud SQL database decoy.
Engine Version: Select a supported version of the database engine.
ACL: Choose your preferred access control list for the cloud SQL database decoy:
Select Public if you want the cloud SQL database decoy to be accessible to anyone.
Select Private if you want the cloud SQL database decoy to be accessible only to internal adversaries.
Region: Select the GCP region in which you want to deploy the decoy.
Password: Enter a root password for the database.
VPC Network Name: Enter the name of the network in the VPC where you want to place the decoy. This option appears only if the ACL value is set to Private.
See image.
Click Save.
If you want to add multiple cloud SQL decoys to GCP, repeat the previous steps for each decoy and then deploy all decoys simultaneously.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings.
Locate the GCP project you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the gcp-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the gcp-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of Google Cloud Storage bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "gcs": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "prefix": "deception/terraform" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same GCP project.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and set the user agent for Terraform:
export TF_APPEND_USER_AGENT="<value_from_ui>"
Run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to export the state file as JSON:
terraform output -json gcp_terraform_output > deployment-output.json
The JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - GCP page, go to Settings, locate the GCP project you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

Upon successful execution of the script, the cloud SQL database decoy is added to GCP. The deployment status is indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the cloud SQL decoys table (Deceive > Cloud Deception > GCP > Cloud SQL) within the Deception Admin Portal. To learn how to configure lures using cloud SQL database decoys, see Configuring Lures Using GCP Decoys.

blocks.text: While removing a PostgreSQL database from the cloud decoy, the following error might occur:

Error, failed to deleteuser postgres in instance <your-decoy-name>: googleapi: Error 400: Invalid request: failed to delete user postgres: . role "postgres" cannot be dropped because some objects depend on it
If the error occurs, follow these steps:

blocks.item: Find the Terraform Resource ID from the state by running following command:
terraform state list
From the result, look for google_sql_user.sql-user-<you-decoy-name>
Copy the Resource ID and run the following command:
terraform state rm <resource_id>
Run the following command:
terraform apply
Deleting the entire instance also deletes the user that can be exploited, so it is considered the safest operation.
